newsitem.title: CANADA: EU may challenge Canada in WTO on PolyGram.
newsitem.headline: EU may challenge Canada in WTO on PolyGram.

text.p: The European Union is considering mounting a WTO challenge of Canada's refusal to let the Dutch firm PolyGram distribute foreign films in Canada, EU Ambassador John Beck said on Wednesday.
Canada last month allowed PolyGram to set up a subsidiary to make films in Canada and distribute them but continued to deny it the right to distribute lucrative foreign films.

PolyGram NV -- 75 percent owned by Philips Electronics NV -- remains dissatisfied, and the European Union is looking at the possibility of taking it to the World Trade Organisation in Geneva, Beck said.

He said the European Commission, the EU's administrative body, was in the process of making a proposal on going to the trade body, although EU Trade Commissioner Leon Brittan would ultimately have to recommend whether to go ahead on the issue at this time.
If he did so, the proposal would go to the European Council of ministers for action.
Beck characterised the Canadian arrangement with PolyGram as insufficient.

He said the EU in general supported Canada's direction on cultural policy -- the concept of trying to protect "culture" from being swamped by foreign content -- but could not accept the discrimination against the EU.
Large Hollywood distributors have been allowed under a "grandfathering" policy to continue distributing American films in Canada.

"What we cannot go along with is the trade effect of such a policy, if you like the side-swiping that happens as a consequence of it to a party that's outside it altogether, which is ourselves," Beck said.
"PolyGram has made it clear to us that by accepting an interim deal with Canada, that's not, as far as it's concerned, the end of the story."
He said the EU could request consultations with Canada under the WTO. If they were unsuccessful, the matter could go to a dispute panel for arbitration or directly to a dispute panel, he said.
